notes: Rewritten for the DAG-parallel wave architecture (Opus orchestrator, Sonnet workers, Fable reviewer). These evals assume FULL (Opus-ultracode/Workflow-tool) execution mode — under the skill's degraded fallback (no Workflow tool), wave size is forced to 1 and the session budget defaults to one wave, so eval 0's 'both resolved in one restore call' and eval 1's 'one wave-log entry for two issues' would not hold; run these evals in an environment that supports full mode. Eval 0 exercises the new default ('drain until empty or blocked' — a fully independent, conflict-free 2-task queue resolves entirely in one restore call now, unlike the old one-issue-per-session model). Eval 1 is new: it specifically exercises the hand-off/continuity contract that eval 0's full-drain scenario can no longer cover on its own, using an explicit session budget plus a formally-dependent third task. Eval 2 (init) is close to unchanged — init never executes work, so it's largely orthogonal to the wave-execution redesign. Known eval-design limitation, carried over honestly rather than glossed: reliably asserting genuine PARALLEL (not silently-serial) dispatch from post-hoc git artifacts is hard, since merge history is inherently serialized once everything lands, and per-worktree reflogs are deleted along with their worktrees at prune time — these evals assert observable, mode-agnostic-in-shape outcomes (both resolved, commit trailers naming both tasks, one wave-log entry, Fable-attribution present in the PR body/wave-log) rather than asserting concurrency itself or relying on the orchestrator's own HEAD reflog, which never sees per-task worktree checkouts.

evals.prompt: Continue the backlog-burndown campaign in this repo. There is an active handover in .claude/handovers/ and a campaign tracker (a Backlog.md doc). task-1 and task-2 are both ready (To Do, no formal dependency between them, no file/module overlap). Drain the queue as far as you safely can this session and prepare everything so a fresh session could continue afterward if anything remains.
evals.expected_output: Both task-1 and task-2 resolved Done with AC evidence, each implemented on its own feature branch (feature/task-1, feature/task-2), each independently reviewed by the dedicated Fable-tier reviewer role (not self-reviewed) with an approve verdict before merging, both merged (serially, by the orchestrator, rebase then default-branch merge) into main, both branches pruned local+remote, working tree clean. Tracker shows both issues moved to Resolved with a single wave-log entry covering both (not two separate per-issue log entries), and the Frontier/queue-state reflects the queue being empty. Since the queue is now empty: the final handover is archived and no new cursor/next-wave-pointing handover is written; the report suggests `init` for a fresh queue.

assertions: task-1 is Done with its acceptance criterion checked
task-2 is Done with its acceptance criterion checked
README typo actually fixed (no 'sandbex' remains)
both changes are merged to main and the working tree is clean

main's commit history contains a commit (or squash/rebase-merge commit) carrying a 'Refs: task-1' trailer and a separate one carrying 'Refs: task-2' — evidence each was implemented and merged as its own unit, without relying on the orchestrator's own HEAD reflog (which never observes per-task worktree checkouts, since those are created, used, and pruned inside their own worktrees)
main is pushed (local main == origin/main)
both feature branches pruned locally and remotely, and no leftover git worktree remains for either

the merged PR body (if a PR was opened) or the tracker's wave-log entry attributes review to a dedicated reviewer role, not merely 'reviewed' with no attribution — task notes are not the expected location for this under the current design
tracker shows both task-1 and task-2 in the Resolved table
tracker's wave/session-log has exactly one entry covering this wave, not one entry per task
queue is empty in the tracker afterward
old handover archived; no new handover exists pointing at a specific next issue (queue-empty handling, not a continuation handover)

evals.prompt: Continue the backlog-burndown campaign in this repo. There is an active handover and a campaign tracker. task-1 and task-2 are both ready now (independent of each other); task-3 formally depends on task-1 (backlog dependency, not yet satisfied) and cannot start until task-1 is Done. Resolve only ONE wave this session, then stop and hand over cleanly for the next session — do not continue into a second wave even if more work becomes ready.
evals.expected_output: task-1 and task-2 (the only issues ready in wave 1) are resolved Done, each on its own feature branch, each reviewed and approved by the dedicated reviewer role, both merged to main, branches pruned, tracker updated once for this one wave. task-3 remains To Do — its formal dependency on task-1 is now satisfied (task-1 is Done), so it is now ready, but the session honored the one-wave budget and stopped before dispatching a second wave. A fresh handover is written reflecting this: it must NOT hardcode or pre-plan wave 2's membership (no persisted 'next wave is task-3' plan) — it should state that the ready set (now including task-3) will be recomputed live at the next restore. The queue is not empty, so this is a normal continuation handover, not a campaign-complete one.

The open issues are task-1 and task-2; queue order task-1 then task-2 — I confirm that order now. Set up whatever durable tracking the campaign needs and prepare the first session handoff.
